clusters.mechanism: Digest seeds review candidates only from PR-opened, round-delivered and approval events, so unread PR activity (e.g. pr.ci_passed) that makes an approval stale is never reconciled against current state.
Digest's awaiting-review predicate ignores review.rounds, so PRs with a running change round are still listed as awaiting review.
Status schema drops run.merged and explainStatus never checks it, so confirmed merged runs are reported as unknown, review needed or otherwise not landed.
The blocked-land branch in explainStatus is evaluated before the closed-PR check, so a closed PR with a historical blocked land is told to retry landing.

privateMatches in the publication gate now decodes repeatedly (including \uXXXX) and returns a synthetic match after 5 rounds, blocking publication even with an empty denylist, which is an unrequested gate change.
When the privacy policy cannot be read, the CallTool handler withholds all tool output, including results of mutations that already ran, so the agent loses the new ids.
Applying the private-strings denylist to every MCP tool's output over-filters, wholesale replacing fields (including short-credential substring hits) in pre-existing tools.
limitless_status omits the constant state and nextAction strings when the privacy policy is unreadable.
Digest fetches run and land details sequentially per distinct run in the SessionStart hook, causing many serial requests.
Approved PRs with no saved prSnapshot are counted as awaiting review because approval.sha !== undefined head is true.
LandQueue.list throws a generic Error for an unknown run, so the HTTP route returns 500 instead of 404.
limitless_review omits the reviewer, so MCP approvals are recorded as reviewer "human" and the audit trail is misattributed.
Digest limits line count but not line length, so long titles, summaries or question text can inject large context.
